text_blocks.snippet: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) are the two main types of lung cancer, differing in their cell structure, growth rate, and treatment approaches. NSCLC is more common, accounting for 80-85% of all lung cancers, and generally grows slower than SCLC. SCLC, while less frequent, is more aggressive and tends to spread more rapidly.
snippet_highlighted_words: NSCLC is more common, accounting for 80-85% of all lung cancers, and generally grows slower than SCLC

list.snippet: Prevalence: NSCLC is far more common than SCLC.
Aggressiveness: SCLC is more aggressive and tends to spread more quickly.
Growth Rate: NSCLC generally grows slower than SCLC.
Treatment: NSCLC is often treated with surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy, while SCLC is typically treated with chemotherapy and radiation.
Prognosis: NSCLC generally has a better prognosis (survival rate) than SCLC, particularly when detected early.

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: NSCLC includes adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Surgery is often a treatment option, especially in early stages. Chemotherapy and radiation are also used.

list.title: Prognosis:
list.snippet: Survival rates vary based on stage, with localized NSCLC having a 63% five-year survival rate according to the Cancer Center.com.

list.title: Types:
list.snippet: SCLC is a distinct type of lung cancer that arises from neuroendocrine cells in the lung.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: SCLC is usually treated with chemotherapy and radiation, as surgery is rarely an option due to its aggressive nature and tendency to spread.

list.title: Prognosis:
list.snippet: SCLC has a poorer prognosis compared to NSCLC, with a lower five-year survival rate.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, while both NSCLC and SCLC are types of lung cancer, their differences in cell type, growth rate, and response to treatment necessitate distinct management strategies.
